newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China, Singapore in $97.5 mln projects in Hebei.
newsitem.headline: China, Singapore in $97.5 mln projects in Hebei.

text.p: Singaporean and Chinese business officials have signed pacts to jointly invest in five projects worth US$97.5 million in the northern Chinese province of Hebei, officials said on Thursday.

"We are confident that more joint venture projects will be signed during Singapore's 1997 International Trade and Industry Fair," said Ma Kai of Hebei province's foreign capital utilisation department.
Ma was among the more than 450 Chinese delegates taking part in the four-day exhibition aimed at promoting Singaporean investment in China.
The five projects include a $63.5 million co-generation power plant, a $5.4 million dairy firm, a $12.5 million real estate project, a $12 million cement factory and a $4.1 million resort, Ma said.
The power plant project would include an investment by Singapore's Keppel FELS Ltd and its China partner Zunhua Energy Development Corporation, Keppel FELS said in a statement.
Keppel FELS said the joint venture would design, construct, commission and operate the 100 megawatt coal-fired plant in the city of Zunhua.
Ma did not detail the other projects but said Singaporean interests would account for nearly 64 percent of the total investments.

China, with 76 exhibitors from the provinces of Hebei, Fujian, Sichuan and the capital Beijing, as well as coastal Shanghai and Guangzhou, was the biggest participant in the 14-nation exhibition which began on Thursday.

"While bringing over 1,500 kinds of commodities to the exhibition here, we will also conduct business talks concerning a large number of carefully-chosen projects that are open for foreign investments," Guo Hongqi, vice governor of Hebei province, said at the opening ceremony.
Hebei hopes to attract foreign investments in a wide range of industries, including infrastructure, electronics, computer, textile and cosmetics, Chinese exhibitors said.
"Singapore has been the most important foreign investor in Hebei. Its total investment was only next to Hong Kong's in 1996," Ma said. He did not give the amount of the investments.
Hebei province, in which Beijing is located, is one of China's major production bases for cereals, cotton and edible oils. It also has substantial mineral resources.
